body: Your best posts are the ones fans could send to one friend. Before you film anything today, name the person a fan would send it to — if you can't, sharpen the idea first.
One Reel today beats three someday. Phone, one take, the Gibson, whatever you're actually working on this morning — raw beats staged in cold-audience testing.
If you post a Reel today, aim for 5–7pm Mountain. That's when your kind of listener is scrolling with time to actually watch.
Monday is your strongest posting day in the current data. If something's ready, don't sit on it until the weekend.
The first 1.5 seconds decide everything. Start mid-strum, mid-sentence, mid-laugh — never with a logo, a title card, or you saying 'hey guys'.
A setlist photo from your last show is a save machine. Fans bookmark what they can use later — and saves are top-tier signal right now.
Today's easiest post: the lyric sheet. A photo of your handwriting with one line about where the song came from earns saves that a polished graphic never will.
Your 'New hair ✂️' post out-reached almost everything last year. That's not an accident — one human moment, three words. You're allowed to do that again today.
If today's post has a TikTok or CapCut watermark on it, don't post it. Re-export clean — the watermark alone can keep it out of Explore entirely.
No link in today's caption. Say 'link in bio' if you need to — the words cost nothing, the clickable URL costs up to half your reach.
Reply to every comment on yesterday's post before you post anything new today. Replies are a ranking signal, not just manners — and they're the cheapest one you have.
Got a show coming up? Make the Facebook Event today and tag the venue. RSVPs compound — the earlier it exists, the more social proof it gathers.
Co-billed show on the calendar? Ask the other artist for an Instagram Collab post — one post, both grids, both audiences. It's the cheapest reach-share in music.
Post your original song clips as their own audio on Instagram. When someone else uses your sound, the algorithm treats your original as culturally relevant — free lift.
Facebook wants volume from you right now — even a two-line show reminder counts. Don't save FB for big announcements; it rewards the steady drip.
Your Facebook crowd is the 35+ Front Range ticket-buyers. Post the show details there today even if it feels repetitive — they're the ones who actually come.
Today's cheapest Reel: 15 seconds of the song you're practicing anyway. You're already holding the guitar — hit record before the third run-through.
One carousel this week should be pure utility: gear rundown, capo chart, the chords to a song you cover. Utility carousels earn 3–4× the saves of a comparable Reel.
If you posted yesterday, spend today's ten minutes in the comments and DMs instead. A day of conversation beats a second mediocre post.
Film today even if you don't post today. Three clips banked on a Tuesday is what makes Thursday's '3–5 Reels a week' possible without panic.
Your EP announcement is still your best-performing post ever — gratitude plus real names tagged. Next milestone, big or small: same recipe.
Sound-off check: could someone get today's Reel with the volume muted? Add the overlay line if not — most first views are silent.
Stories are where the link lives. New song out, tickets on sale — put the link sticker in a Story today and keep the caption clean.
A voice memo of a half-written verse is a post. Fans fund the process, not just the product — let them hear the song before it's finished.
Today, answer one question a fan actually asked you — in a Reel, to camera, thirty seconds. Real questions are pre-validated hooks.
If you're driving to a gig today, the merch table setup, the empty room, the soundcheck — that's three Stories and a Reel. The show documents itself if you let it.
Don't ask people to comment, tag friends, or 'like if you agree' today or any day. Meta demotes bait — and it drags the whole account's trust, not just the post.
Post the cover song clip, but check the first three seconds land on the line everyone knows. Familiarity is the hook; your voice is the reason they stay.
Two weeks out from a show is Event-push day one. Final week is push two. In between, let the Event sit — two touches, not seven.
The sofa is your set. The EP is literally named for it — when you don't know where to film today, film there. Fans recognize home.
Batch your captions when the coffee's still hot. Three captions written in one sitting sound like you; three written at 11pm before posting sound like a press release.
If today's idea feels too small to post, it's probably the right size. At your reach, one honest moment beats one produced announcement every time.
Check your Professional Dashboard's 'Best Time to Post' once a month, not every day. Benchmarks got you started; your own audience data gets the final word.
New original out? Clip the most singable eight seconds and release it as its own audio today. That clip is the ad; the audio page is the funnel.
One photo of the crowd from the stage says more than any 'thanks for coming' graphic. Post the room, tag the venue, name one moment that surprised you.
Today's Reel doesn't need a concept. Tune the Gibson on camera and talk about the song you're about to practice. Process is content.
If a post is doing better than usual right now, stay at the table — reply to every comment within the hour. Momentum compounds while the post is still being tested.
Never let a reaction or commentary clip go up without your actual take in it. Meta deprioritizes bare reactions — your two cents is what makes it yours.
Post the same clean Reel to Facebook natively today — don't just share the Instagram link. Native FB Reels are the fastest growth lever that platform has right now.
The 'boring' post you're avoiding — rehearsal, string change, coffee before writing — is the one that makes fans feel like insiders. Ship one this week.
When you announce anything today, lead with the feeling, not the fact. 'I cried mixing this one' beats 'New single out Friday' — the fact goes in sentence two.
Three-clip minimum before you leave any venue: the room empty, one song moment, one crowd or merch-table moment. Future-you will thank you on a slow content week.
Ask the venue to co-post or Collab your show announcement. Their followers are your town's live-music regulars — exactly who you can't reach alone.
If you've posted three Reels this week already, today is a rest day or a carousel day. The cadence target is 3–5 — six is not a bonus round.
The caption question that gets real replies is specific: 'What's the first concert you ever cried at?' — not 'What do you think?' Specific questions are answerable in one thumb-line.
Your fans' covers, dances, or uses of your audio: reshare one today if it exists. Nothing signals 'this artist is happening' like other people holding your song.
Weekday mid-morning (9–11am MT) is a solid window for a Feed photo or carousel. Save the evenings for Reels — different formats, different clocks.
Once a month, pin your best recent post to the top of your grid. New listeners judge the whole account by the first three tiles.
The gear question you get asked most — answer it once, properly, as a carousel. Then you have a save-magnet and a place to point every future asker.
Before a cover song post, write one line about why this song, why you, why now. That line is the difference between a karaoke clip and a Meghan post.
If today's the day before a show, your only job is one Reel: 'tomorrow night, this room, these songs' — fifteen seconds, venue tagged, Event linked in Stories.
End the week by reading your own last five captions out loud. If one doesn't sound like you talking to a friend at the merch table, that's the register to fix next week.
